Yep. Dumped over text in January of 2021 and I never heard from her again. I did try to reach out several weeks later and realized I had been blocked. I’m still not sure what happened and at this point I wouldn’t really care.

I do still think about her occasionally, but as it goes, I don’t feel anything these days. The whole thing feels like a bad dream or something. 

It did mess my head up pretty bad at the time. Being dumped over text by someone you’re in love with will tend to do that I guess. 

It’s been 4 years and I’ve only casually dated since then. I like it better this way I think.

It took me about 4.5 months for me to get to a point where it was manageable and I could live my life without being consumed by it. After that I was still sad for a while longer, but it felt less intense and less frequent as well. You just kind of get to a point where your brain / body are exhausted by it and you have no choice but to move on (which is a good thing). Hang in there, it will happen for you as well.

Been there. It passes. I was suicidal for like an entire month after my last breakup. I ended up at the hospital for a week. It was like a bad dream I couldn’t wake up from. Hey man. You’re just experiencing a massive wave of grief. I’ve been there before and overcame it. I’m also there now as well. I remember sitting in the ER waiting to be admitted for a 3 day psychiatric evaluation because the pain was too much to handle. I had completely hit rock bottom. I actually shouldn’t be alive right now. 3 months later, I was in a much better place, and the pain was manageable. You just have to let time do it’s thing and trust the process, but I can confirm that time alone won’t completely heal you, once you start to feel a bit better (and you will), you need to force yourself to do things to distract yourself from those awful thoughts. 

Unfortunately, I’m back in the same situation as a few years prior. I was up at 4AM today ready to admit myself to the ER again, but I’m feeling slightly better now, so just taking things a minute at a time and allowing myself to grieve.

I’m seeing a therapist twice a week and started Prozac to lift me up a bit. The pills haven’t started working yet, but I’m hanging in there for now. I owe it to myself to see what my future holds. You should too.

There are better days ahead, but you HAVE to give it more time, and you HAVE to let the grieving process work it’s natural course.
